flawed_step: The key step of any proof would be: "since the arc capacities are pairwise distinct, no two different s-t cuts can have the same capacity." This does not follow. A cut's capacity is a sum over a set of arcs, and two different vertex sets S can cross exactly the same set of arcs. That happens, for example, when a vertex has no arcs (isolated vertices are allowed), so adding it to S or leaving it out changes nothing.
counterexample: Take V = {s,a,b,t} with a single arc s->t of capacity 1, so a and b are isolated. The maximum flow is 1 > 0. The cuts {s}, {s,a}, {s,b} and {s,a,b} all have capacity 1, so there are four minimum cuts. Isolated vertices are not even needed: with arcs s->a (1) and a->t (2), b has no arcs, and both {s} and {s,b} are minimum cuts of capacity 1.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. I tried to prove uniqueness, but distinct arc capacities only make sums of different arc sets differ in special cases. They cannot separate two different vertex sets that cross the same arcs. With 4 vertices and a vertex that has no arcs, adding or removing that vertex from S leaves the cut's capacity unchanged. So there is more than one minimum cut, even though the maximum flow is positive.
